transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 50 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Lena Martinez (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood SRE); Maya Patel (Acuity Head of ML), Tom Rogers (Acuity Infra Lead), Priya Singh (Acuity Security), Evan Lee (Acuity DevOps)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
- Pilot cluster remains stable; intermittent routing errors during high-concurrency runs.
- Networking config (VPC peering + SG rules) needs small change; customer to share flow logs.
- Redwood SE to deploy kernel/quantization patch to test nodes; benchmarks next week.
- Security items: KMS integration questions and audit log fields to confirm.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give it a few secs for people to pop in, but we've got a pretty tight agenda today: routing issues, benchmark results, and the on-prem upgrade window.
[00:18] Maya: sounds good, thanks Lena. I see most of the folks here.
[00:24] Tom: yeah quick note, we had one of the dev boxes flake yesterday during the 1k ramp, ended up dropping about 3% of requests, not sure if that's network or runtime.
[00:35] Devon: ok good to call out; we've reproduced something similar in our lab when simulating burst concurrency with longer context lengths. suspect it's a combination of the peering MTU + K-V cache warmup.
[00:50] Priya: when you say K-V cash, you mean the KV cache in the inference runtime? I heard cash which made me think billing :)
[00:58] Devon: yeah sorry, KV cache. transcriber is being helpful.
[01:05] Samir: quick infra note — when the pilot was first provisioned we saw a mismatch in the route table for the subnets in us-east-1 that caused some traffic to route via the transit gateway instead of the direct peering. fixed one rule but a residual exists for the worker subnets.
[01:25] Tom: right that's the one we patched last week, might be something else still. Evan can share the flow logs.
[01:32] Evan: yep I'll export and drop in the shared folder after the meeting.
[01:36] Lena: great, next up benchmarks — Devon you ran the batch tests on the quantized build?
[01:42] Devon: yes — patched the model runtime with the newer kernel selection heuristics. Results on the test cluster: 18% lower p50 latency for 2k token prompts, throughput improved ~22% under our synthetic load. but under multi-tenancy bursts we saw tail spikes.
[01:58] Maya: can you share the CSV and the exact flags you used? we need to reproduce with our prompt set.
[02:05] Devon: absolutely, I'll drop the CSV. flags were --kernel-autoselect, --kv-prefetch enabled, and quantize mode q4_0; note that q4_0 had slight drop in token quality for one of our eval prompts (more hallucination), so we're also testing q5_0 on accuracy-for-larger-context.
[02:30] Tom: on the network side, we noticed packet fragmentation when MTU wasn't aligned; could that cause request retries that look like dropped tokens?
[02:39] Samir: yes fragmentation can cause retransmits and trigger our connection pool backoffs; that shows up as higher tail latency.
[02:46] Priya: any implications for our audit logs or packet capture — do we need deeper retention for the trial?
[02:54] Lena: good Q. Redwood can accept flow logs and we can correlate request ids, but for full packet capture you'd need to provide pcap from your side; we don't ship raw pcaps.
[03:06] Priya: okay fair. we also need to confirm KMS key usage — will Redwood reach to our KMS for model artifacts or only for request encryption keys?
[03:15] Devon: currently the pilot uses customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption of logs (S3), and for transit we support TLS with certs you control. full KMS integration for runtime keying (in-ram encryption) is on our roadmap; we'll scope what fields you need in audit first.
[03:34] Maya: timeline-wise how long to get the kernel patch out to our nodes? last week you said by mid next week?
[03:40] Devon: we can push to the test pool within 48 hours, but for the on-prem nodes we need the maintenance window — we don't force restarts outside agreed times.
[03:50] Lena: action: Devon will push test kernel to the pilot test pool. (note: this is a verbal action item).
[03:56] Tom: one more note — our infra team wants to avoid opening wide CIDR ranges; are there specific IP ranges Redwood needs for the dedicated control plane connections?
[04:05] Lena: yes we'll send the precise list. we recommend using the peering route plus a small set of egress IPs.
[04:12] Evan: i'll hold on that, we prefer explicit IP sets over open SGs.
[04:17] Lena: perfect. next, the intermittent routing errors: can you walk us through the most recent incident log, Tom?
[04:24] Tom: sure — 2026-04-14 03:12 UTC, we saw a spike in 502/connection reset on a subset of workers. flow logs show a retransmit backlog, and our kube-proxy logs show NAT table entries being evicted under load.
[04:38] Samir: kube-proxy evictions could be due to conntrack limits; we suggested increasing conntrack max, and also adjusting the LB idle timeout.
[04:47] Priya: conntrack changes require security sign-off; can we get a minimal change plan?
[04:52] Samir: yes, bump from default 65536 to 131072, monitor for 24 hours, rollback plan ready.
[04:58] Maya: do we have any SLA impact if we do this during business hours?
[05:03] Lena: we'd prefer maintenance window; otherwise we can route low-traffic tests during night.
[05:08] Tom: we can do midnight UTC window next Tuesday (2026-04-21) if that works for Redwood.
[05:14] Devon: that should be fine; Redwood SE + SRE will be on-call.
[05:18] Priya: also want to confirm audit trails for any config changes — we need to sign off on every infra change during the pilot.
[05:25] Lena: understood, we'll document everything in the change request and add git diffs and runbooks.
[05:31] Maya: on the security docs — Lena, you mentioned a short pack earlier?
[05:35] Lena: yes, I'll send the SOC 2 + network runbook and a summary of KMS capabilities. expect that today.
[05:41] Priya: great. regarding data residency, we need assurances logs don't leave region unencrypted; what's Redwood's current behavior?
[05:49] Devon: logs written to your S3 with customer-managed keys remain in your region; Redwood's control plane calls are minimal and instrumented — we can provide a breakdown of which call types are sent outside region.
[06:02] Tom: hopping back to benchmarks — when you ran the multi-tenant stress test, did you isolate per-tenant token budgets? we saw one tenant gobble cache and starve others.
[06:13] Devon: in that test we used fair-share batching but the KV cache is currently shared; for the pilot we enabled prefix isolation which limits cache eviction blowouts. that reduced inter-tenant tail by ~60%.
[06:28] Maya: we'll need to reproduce with our actual prompt mix; please include prefix isolation flags in the CSV.
[06:35] Devon: will do.
[06:37] Evan: quick ops Q — any network ports we should whitelist for health checks?
[06:41] Samir: only standard HTTPS and a small set of high ports for health probes, i'll include them in the diagram.
[06:47] Tom: about upgrades — is there a recommended order: control plane first, runtime next? we want minimal downtime.
[06:54] Lena: recommended: 1) test pool patch, 2) validate perf/accuracy, 3) staged rollout to workers with canary, and 4) control plane changes last.
[07:06] Maya: what are the rollback mechanics if quantization causes quality regressions?
[07:12] Devon: rollback is automatic per-deployment flag; we also keep model version pins so you can return to exact binary. runtime state will flush caches on rollback so warmup may be slower for a bit.
[07:24] Priya: we'll need the evals you ran; can you attach the prompt set and outputs?
[07:30] Devon: yes, we'll push the eval set and outputs to the shared folder. note one of the prompts had increased hallucination at q4_0 — that's why we're testing q5_0.
[07:41] Lena: jump to timeline — we have the maintenance window proposed week of 2026-04-27. is that still acceptable?
[07:48] Tom: yes that works, assuming we finalize the change list prior.
[07:52] Maya: also, can Redwood support a short live benchmark during the window — we can run a 30-minute load test after patching?
[07:59] Devon: yes, Redwood can coordinate a quick smoke and then a 30-min soak. we'll need explicit go/no-go criteria which we can draft.
[08:09] Evan: criteria: p50 within 10% of baseline, error rate < 0.5%, and tail p99 under 5x baseline.
[08:19] Samir: agreed.
[08:21] Lena: good. any procurement/legal blockers?
[08:25] Maya: procurement expects updated addendum for pilot extension; legal is reviewing the data residency clauses.
[08:31] Lena: I can follow up with contracts.
[08:33] Priya: on KMS keys — we need to see the specific audit fields Redwood stores (request_id, user, action, timestamp).
[08:41] Devon: we'll provide a list today.
[08:44] Tom: last technical note — we saw a spike when model checkpointing hit disk IO saturation; is there a recommended ephemeral storage size for workers?
[08:54] Samir: recommend 500GB ephemeral with io1/ io2-like throughput; also tune checkpoint frequency during heavy inference.
[09:03] Maya: ok we'll adjust.
[09:06] Lena: ok let's recap and confirm action items.
[09:10] Lena: Devon to push kernel patch to test pool and run 1k request benchmark — due 2026-04-17.
[09:17] Lena: Tom/Evan to share VPC flow logs and SG rules — due 2026-04-20.
[09:22] Lena: Priya to confirm KMS audit fields needed — due 2026-04-22.
[09:27] Lena: Lena will send SOC2 pack and network runbook + IP list — due 2026-04-16.
[09:31] Maya: can we also get a quick one-page runbook for the rollback steps?
[09:35] Lena: yes will include.
[09:37] Devon: I'll also attach the CSV with the exact flags and the eval outputs.
[09:41] Tom: maintenance window target week of 2026-04-27, exact date TBD after logs.
[09:46] Lena: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up via the shared Confluence page and I'll email the runbook and pricing outline.
[09:53] Maya: thanks all.
[09:55] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional misrecognitions (e.g., KV cash), some filler words, speaker overlap at two points. Links shared: /shared/acuity-pilot/flow-logs (placeholder), /shared/acuity-pilot/benchmarks/patch-results.csv (placeholder).
